chapter: Stuff Smith, 52nd Street and session work
title: 1930s session work: how dates were booked and what they paid
summary: Leaders asked him at the club; three-hour sessions paid about $45-50.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Mildred Bailey, Red Norvo, Joe Marsella, oh yeah, Red Norvo, Lionel, Ella, of course Sarah, Sarah Vaughn, the Andrews Sisters, yeah, I did a lot of recordings.
How were those record dates arranged? Did they just tell you to show up at the studio at such and such a time?

Yeah, well they would come by the club you know wherever you'd be working and they say 'would you like to do a record date with me next Monday or whenever'. And you would look at your schedule. Yes. And they'd tell you just what studio and time and that was it. You'd go do it. It was just a record date.
Were the sessions three hours then?
Yeah, same as now, sometimes you'd have to
four tunes in the three hours.
I think it was then $45.00, something like that, $50.00. I forget the exact amount then. But it was good money then.
